01

Available now · Complete two-volume edition

Takanas
HaShavin

The Remedy of the Penitents Rav Tzadok’s sustained exploration of what teshuvah can heal—and what it can remake.

What if return does more than erase failure?

What if it can change the meaning of what came before?

Across fifteen simanim, Rav Tzadok follows teshuvah from healing and the Throne of Glory to love, fear, atonement, and complete repair. The original Hebrew, interlinear English, and sources remain together on every page.

02

Available now · A bilingual edition

The Livyasan
and Shavuos

From the deep to the hidden light. A symbol appearing at the climax of Akdamus becomes a map of Torah, revelation, and the world to come.

Why does Akdamus place the Livyasan at the summit of Shavuos?

The answer moves through Gemara, Zohar, Arizal, Rav Tzadok, and the Izhbitza-Radzin dynasty.

The future seudah, Torah Sheb’al Peh, divine laughter, Yam Suf, and the hidden light are not scattered images. This volume follows their connections until they gather into one unfolding teaching.

Part I · Foundations

The sources beneath the symbol

Bava Basra, Avodah Zarah, Akdamus, Yetziv Pisgam, Zohar, and the Arizal.

Part II · Rav Tzadok

A constellation of teachings

Tzidkat HaTzaddik, Pri Tzaddik, Likutei Maamarim, and Machshavos Charutz.

Part III · Izhbitza-Radzin

The inheritance crosses generations

Mei HaShiloach, Beis Yaakov, and Sod Yesharim carry the teaching forward.

Part IV · Synthesis

The passages become one

An influence map and six themes bring the entire journey into focus.

Coming soon · A complete two-volume edition

Dover
Tzedek

Rav Tzadok’s running commentary on the Talmud. A close reading of the sugya becomes an ascent through halachah, aggadah, Kabbalah, and the inner life.

Coming soon

What if a line of Gemara is not the endpoint, but the doorway?

In Eruvin, separate domains become a drama of multiplicity gathered into the domain of the One.

The complete edition is divided into two substantial 7×10 volumes. The original Hebrew remains visible, the English follows phrase by phrase, and the footnotes trace the sources and parallel teachings that illuminate Rav Tzadok’s movement of thought.
